only 37 % of the domain is free for the optimiser to decide.
preserve is 72 % of the expected final part (127953 mm3 of 178389 mm3 at volfrac 0.05). Most of this shape is drawn, not optimised; say so wherever the result is presented.

the free region is only 2.0 voxels (6.00 mm) thick at its thinnest. Below about 3 voxels there is no room for a hole, so the topology there is set by the outline rather than chosen -- refine the grid or widen the design space.

the free region's median thickness is 6.00 mm, below the 9.00 mm filter radius. The filter cannot form a member narrower than itself, so most of the free region will come out grey and the threshold, not the optimisation, will decide what is material.

the 6 support point(s) are fixed by preserve at knuckles at [-71.7, 9.8, 100.4]; latch_lo at [63.2, 22.2, 40.5]; latch_hi at [63.2, 22.2, 169.5]; pocket_bot at [1.6, 41.5, -10.2]; band_mid at [1.9, 39.6, 100.5]; pocket_top at [1.9, 39.8, 209.6]. Where the part is held is an input to this study, not a result of it -- if the layout of the supports is itself meant to be optimised, that decision is currently being made in CAD.

build_volume.voxel_vs_min_feature: one voxel is 3.00 mm and the smallest printable wall is 0.80 mm, so the grid cannot represent the printer's limit; minimum-feature checks on this run are about the grid, not the machine.

design_freedom.note_fixed_points: 11 load/support footprint(s) sit on preserve at positions the CAD model chose. The optimiser decides how to reach them, not where they are.

multigrid.precision: mixed (float32 cycle, float64 coarse solve and outer CG)

runtime_estimate.basis: one cold conjugate-gradient solve of load case 1 at uniform density, times cases times iterations. Warm starting makes later iterations cheaper; continuation towards a 0/1 field makes them dearer. Measured runs land within 0.5x - 1.5x.
